coinflix.html:
Case Study: Coinflix - The Blockchain-Powered Entertainment Platform

Project Overview:

Coinflix represents a pioneering fusion of entertainment and blockchain technology, drawing inspiration from industry giants like Netflix, Axie Infinity, and TikTok. By tokenizing micro shows from creators and leveraging blockchain infrastructure, Coinflix revolutionizes content consumption and creator monetization. With a vision to disrupt the traditional entertainment landscape, Coinflix has emerged as a frontrunner in the burgeoning realm of blockchain-based media platforms.

Problem Statement:

In today's digital age, content creators often face challenges related to monetization, intellectual property rights, and audience engagement. Moreover, conventional entertainment platforms struggle to offer creators transparent revenue-sharing models and direct interaction with their audience.

Challenges:

  1. Develop a platform that empowers content creators to monetize their creations seamlessly through blockchain technology.
  2. Implement innovative features akin to TikTok's short-form video format to captivate audiences and enhance user engagement.
  3. Establish a vibrant community of creators and consumers, fostering collaboration, interaction, and content discovery.

Design Process:

Discover Phase:

  • Quantitative Research: Conducted user surveys to glean insights into user preferences and pain points within the entertainment landscape.
    • Discovered a growing demand for decentralized content platforms offering fair compensation to creators.
    • Identified a preference for short-form, immersive content experiences akin to TikTok's format.

Competitive Analysis:

  • Evaluated existing entertainment platforms and blockchain-based projects to identify market gaps and potential areas for innovation.
  • Recognized the need to integrate elements of social media interaction, gaming dynamics, and decentralized finance to create a multifaceted entertainment ecosystem.

Define Phase:

  • Developed personas and user journey maps to empathize with the needs and aspirations of content creators and consumers.

Ideation Phase:

  • Brainstormed ideas for platform features, content formats, and monetization mechanisms to align with user expectations and market trends.

Design Phase:

  • Paper Sketches: Generated initial concepts and interface layouts to visualize key features and interactions.
  • Low-fidelity Wireframes: Created basic wireframes outlining the structure and flow of the platform.
  • Mid-fidelity Wireframes: Iterated on wireframes, incorporating feedback and refining user flows for optimal usability.
  • Final Design: Produced high-fidelity designs integrating blockchain elements, interactive features, and immersive content experiences.

Key UI Solutions:

  • Short-Form Content Feed: Curated feed showcasing micro shows and short-form videos from creators, fostering engagement and content discovery.
  • Tokenized Rewards System: Implemented blockchain-based rewards for creators and consumers, incentivizing quality content creation and consumption.
  • Social Interaction Features: Integrated social media-like features such as likes, comments, and shares to facilitate community interaction and content virality.
  • Creator Dashboard: Empowered creators with insights into audience engagement, earnings, and performance metrics, enhancing transparency and accountability.

Key Audience:

Coinflix appeals to a diverse audience comprising content creators, entertainment enthusiasts, blockchain enthusiasts, and individuals seeking novel ways to engage with digital content. However, the platform's primary audience includes:

  • Content Creators: Artists, filmmakers, influencers, and creators seeking a fair and transparent platform to showcase their talent and monetize their creations.
  • Entertainment Enthusiasts: Consumers passionate about discovering and consuming engaging content across various genres and formats.
  • Blockchain Enthusiasts: Individuals intrigued by the intersection of entertainment and blockchain technology, eager to explore innovative platforms and decentralized ecosystems.

Takeaways:

Coinflix represents a paradigm shift in the entertainment landscape, leveraging blockchain technology to democratize content creation, distribution, and monetization. By embracing principles of decentralization, transparency, and community empowerment, Coinflix is poised to redefine the future of entertainment, one micro show at a time.

lumio-couples.title: Product Case I: 🇬🇧 Lumio / Couples Spending. JTBD-approach
lumio-couples.html:
Results

  • 200,000+ connected accounts analysing data from £3.5 bn of transactions
  • Customer base grew up nearly 400% & daily use up 216% in past 12 months, now reaching 34.7k active users
  • Recognised on a list of “Top Money Apps-2023” – Metro

My Role

Product Designer

Jan 2022 - Now

I led design from start to finish, from conducting research, establishing development processes, creating brand identity, UX, UI, testing and pushing to product hunt and invesment market.

Background

Lumio was building a hyper personalised finance app for people to grow their money on autopilot. Since working with ex-Paypal director & 500 Startups VC Matt Lerner, Lumio was recognised as one of Metro's top money managing apps, alongside Monzo, Moneybox & Chip. At this time we recognized a major need and opportunity in the couple finance market, so I was invited as a Lead Designer to make this switch.

Case Description

In this case I describe how I helped Lumio succesfully switch from Saving money on autopilot to Couples Finances market, to become couple-oriented product, for money management within couple.

Achievements

Raised Sign Up rate on 9% from 89,7% to 98,04%

The process. Discover & Define Stage

  1. Identifying the market. Desk Research

My first step was that I learned everything I found about a world of couples finances. I gathered and read more than 25 different articles and researches about couples finance management, mostly in UK.

  1. Formulate JTBDs

After analyzing the data, I facilitated cross-functional workshop, on which potential Jobs to be Done for couples were generated. In total we generated 7 Macro JTBDs. In the same time I reached to existing customer base and scheduled 35 interviews with users who identified themselves as a couple members. We decided to use interviews to evaluate and validate ideas.

  1. Interviews Preparation

For interviews I made scripts, covering:

  • Who they are
  • their motivations
  • their needs and solutions they are after
  • JTBD validation
  1. Interview Analysis

In the end we had 32 interviews, which I analysed and broken down, using this data for this and another cases. Based on this data, we realised that most important are keeping track of couple’s money from different bank accounts, and easily managing shared expenses.

Image: Micro JTBDs of the JTBD-1

  1. Competitors Research

I made very specific and narrow Competitors research - based on how our competitors performing Micro tasks of our customers.

  1. Prioritisation

As soon as we have very limited resources and small team, I had to narrow our work focus to get the quickest win possible. In process of interview analysis, I realised that our users have way more request for managing shared spending.

Ideation Stage

  1. Solution for managing shared spending

I organised series of cross-team workshops used the certain techiniques to engage the full team participation in ideation stage. In order to get ideas for MicroJTBDs, used a NN-group Storyboard technique.

I added all data that was relevant, and asked team to proceed.

  1. Analysis and breakdown of proposed solutions.

We focused on design solutions that can ease shared spending management, such as: Sharing transactions, setting Shared recurring costs, spending breakdown chart and even Tracker of who owes what.

  1. Prioritisation

I have performed prioritisation using the Wow-How-Now matrix. Each team member engaged in production, evaluated effort and possible value at such an early stage. The most expensive in terms of development ideas were also moved to backlog, and the most valuable, and fast in implementation were planned to the next stage.

  1. Results +Evaluation

I engaged the full dev team both Front and back end to evaluate efforts from their side to make sure the solutions we proposed will be not only effective but also within the timetable and framework of budget. Ideas that did not fit for NOW and NEXT - went to backlog.

DO NOW:

DO NEXT:

IDEAS BACKLOG:

Development phase

  1. Describing ideas

As long as I have already developed full scalable token based design system, I have focused on flows and UX build. I skip lo-fi prototypes stage because I build prototypes using blocks from Lumio design system

  1. UX-Part

Next, I mapped out experience and local architecture of new features

  1. UI-Part

As long as I have developed token-based, atomic design system, I usually skip the mid-fi prototyping phase, and usually jump from very lo-fidelity prototypes to the almost-high fidelity prototypes which we can quickly test.

Outcomes

📊 Pie Chart Overview: Enabled users to seeexpense distributions with a visual pie chart breakdown among collaborators.
👥 Collaborator Cards: Added spending cards for each contributor, showcasing their spending contributions (transactions). We imlemented possibility to individually share or hide any transaction from any account
💡 Payment Projection: We enabled users to anticipate future expenses with the introduction of Upcoming Payments on the Spending tab.
🔍 Payment Indicators: We enhanced transaction transparency with clear indicators within the transaction details view, and integrated labels to denote the account utilized for each payment, facilitating efficient tracking.

Development

Designs were passed to the development with all necessary instructions. In general for this particular task I provided more than 14 prototypes (I usually make microprototypes for developers to ensure smooth understanding), more than 200 screens and updated Design System with new elements.

Testing

I have also written down test cases and made all team perform them on test accounts before dropping things live.

…my work never stops as I am always working with feedback and making improvements💘

trucking.html:
Understanding User Needs

Key Audiences

Our primary audience comprises truck drivers, tasked with navigating pickups, deliveries, and managing various logistical aspects on the go. Their work environments are dynamic, often involving remote locations, fluctuating connectivity, and time-sensitive tasks.

Specifics of Work

  • Pickup and Delivery Management: Drivers are responsible for collecting and delivering loads, recording crucial information at each location.
  • Companion Functionality: Fuel purchases, vehicle inspections, and in-app chat facilitate seamless operations.
  • Offline Usage: Since drivers operate in areas with limited connectivity, the app must prioritize offline functionality.

Design Assets

To align with our company's branding while charting a new course, we sought inspiration from our corporate landing page and avoided replicating the style of the legacy app. Our design assets included logos, colors, and style guides, ensuring consistency with our brand identity. THIS IS THE BEFORE - what client came to me with

Platform and Screen Considerations

For the initial release, we targeted iOS iPads, with subsequent plans for Android compatibility. Responsive design was crucial, with a focus on screen sizes suitable for iPads and potential future adaptation to smartphones.

Designing the Solution

Core Functionality

The redesigned app encompassed essential features:

  1. Pickup and Delivery Management: Streamlined interfaces guided drivers through arrival, load management, and departure processes. Ability to quickly confirm or decline new pickup
  1. Ability to review load before starting the trip, and then - during the trip

3. Contact Management:

As a driver I need to be able to add/edit/remove a contact from a pickup/drop details when I learn about a new one.

Contact = Name + multiple phone numbers

Attached mockup by client only showed an idea for the "add" button.

My result:

3. Tank Management: Tailored tank sections allowed drivers to manage multiple tanks efficiently, with intuitive gauging options for different methods.

  1. Duration Tracking: Detailed duration sections captured essential metrics like arrival time, load duration, and wait times, crucial for billing and efficiency monitoring.
  1. Media Attachments: Drivers could easily attach photos or videos, including receipts and general media, enhancing documentation and communication.
  1. Error Handling: Robust error handling mechanisms, including field-level validation and general error messages, ensured data accuracy and user guidance.

Also, there were a lot of other tasks, which I guess will be too boring for you to review due to their complexity. But reach to me so I can show you them on a call

Approach:

Discover Phase:

  • Quantitative Research: Conducted user surveys and market analysis to gain insights into user preferences, pain points, and industry trends.
    • Discovered a growing demand for platforms offering exclusive content and direct interactions between creators and fans.
    • Identified a need for innovative monetization mechanisms and community-building features within fan communities.

Competitive Analysis:

  • Evaluated existing platforms catering to fan communities, subscription-based content models, and interactive social media features.
  • Identified gaps and opportunities for differentiation, focusing on enhancing user engagement, creator monetization, and community dynamics.

Define Phase:

  • Developed personas, empathy maps, and user journey maps to understand user behaviors, motivations, and pain points thoroughly.

Ideation Phase:

  • Brainstormed ideas for platform features, revenue streams, and engagement mechanisms, leveraging insights from user research and competitive analysis.

Design Phase (My part):

  • Week-by-Week Plan: As the design lead, I formulated a comprehensive week-by-week plan outlining design milestones, tasks, and deliverables, ensuring alignment with project goals and timelines.
  • Design System Creation: Led the creation of a robust design system encompassing UI components, visual styles, interaction patterns, and brand guidelines. This design system served as a foundational framework for maintaining consistency and scalability across the platform.

Key UI Solutions:

  • Exclusive Content Feeds: Curated feeds showcasing exclusive content from creators, incentivizing fan subscriptions and recurring revenue.
  • Paid Interactions: Implemented paid interaction features such as virtual gifts, premium comments, and personalized messages to enhance creator monetization and fan engagement.
  • Audio Chatrooms: Introduced audio chatrooms for real-time interactions between creators and fans, fostering community engagement and connection.
  • Community Building Tools: Integrated community-building features such as forums, polls, and events to facilitate interaction and collaboration within fan communities.
  1. Review and Analysis: I started by thoroughly reviewing the existing UI-kit and designs to understand its structure and components.
  2. Identification of Unique Components: I meticulously analyzed the provided Figma files to identify any new or unique design elements that were not part of the existing library.
  3. Integration: The next step involved integrating the identified unique components into the existing design system. This required careful consideration of design principles and consistency.
  4. Documentation: To ensure clarity and usability, I provided comprehensive documentation outlining the usage guidelines, variations, and specifications of each integrated component.

    Implementation:

  1. Extracting Unique Components: I extracted unique design elements such as buttons, icons, typography styles, and UI components from the provided Figma files.
  2. Integration with Existing Library: These extracted components were then seamlessly integrated into the existing design system, ensuring consistency and coherence.
  3. Documentation: I documented each component's purpose, usage guidelines, variations, and specifications to facilitate easy reference for designers and developers.

    Results:

  1. Enhanced Design System: By integrating new components, the design system was enriched, providing designers with a wider range of options to choose from.
  2. Streamlined Design Process: The comprehensive design system streamlined the design process, enabling designers to work more efficiently and effectively.
  3. Improved Consistency: With a unified design system, consistency across projects was improved, enhancing the overall quality of the agency's work.

    Conclusion:

    By successfully consolidating unique design components from the provided Figma files into the existing design system, I helped the client enhance their design capabilities and streamline their workflow. The comprehensive design system now serves as a valuable resource for the agency, ensuring consistency, efficiency, and high-quality design output.

projector.title: My Students’ work: 🇺🇦 Projector Mobile Interfaces
projector.html:
Project Overview:

In this project, I had the pleasure of guiding my students through the process of designing a mobile application from scratch as part of their coursework. Over the duration of the course, they were tasked with conceptualizing and developing a full-fledged mobile app as if they were launching their own startup. This project allowed them to apply the principles and techniques they learned throughout the course to solve real-world problems and create impactful user experiences.

Problem Statement:

The students were challenged to identify a problem that could be addressed through a mobile application and formulate a solution that resonated with potential users. They had the freedom to choose their own topics or select from a list provided. The key was to focus on a problem that was both familiar and intriguing to them, ensuring they remained engaged and motivated throughout the design process.

Design Process:

The design process began with extensive research and ideation sessions where students explored various problem areas and brainstormed potential solutions. They then translated their ideas into concrete concepts, refining and iterating upon them based on feedback and user testing. Throughout this phase, they utilized design thinking methodologies to ensure their solutions were not only feasible but also desirable and viable.

Student Coursework Deliverables:

1. iOS Guidelines Exploration:

  • During this session, students delved into the principles and guidelines governing iOS app design. They gained insights into Apple's design philosophy and best practices for creating intuitive and user-friendly interfaces.

2. Material Design Principles Study:

  • In this module, students explored Google's Material Design principles, focusing on the use of color, typography, and motion to create cohesive and visually appealing experiences across different platforms and devices.

3. Design Process Workshop:

  • This session provided students with an overview of the design process, from initial research and ideation to prototyping and testing. They learned how to approach design challenges systematically and iteratively to achieve optimal results.

4. User Flow Analysis:

  • Students examined the flow of interactions within digital products, emphasizing the importance of understanding user journeys and designing intuitive navigation paths to enhance user experience.

5. Navigation Design Techniques:

  • During this module, students explored various navigation patterns and techniques used in digital interfaces, learning how to design efficient and user-centric navigation systems that facilitate seamless interaction.

6. Patterns Exploration (Part 1):

  • This session focused on identifying and applying common design patterns and components in interface design, enabling students to leverage established conventions to improve usability and consistency.

7. Form Design Principles:

  • Students learned how to design effective and user-friendly forms, considering factors such as layout, labeling, and input validation to optimize form completion and minimize user errors.

8. Typography Fundamentals:

  • In this module, students explored the principles of typography, including font selection, hierarchy, and readability. They gained an understanding of how typography contributes to the overall visual appeal and usability of digital interfaces.

9. Visual Design Principles Exploration:

  • During this session, students examined fundamental principles of visual design, such as balance, contrast, and alignment. They learned how to apply these principles to create visually compelling and harmonious designs.

10. Patterns Exploration (Part 2):

  • Building on their previous exploration of design patterns, students delved deeper into advanced patterns and interactions, learning how to innovate and adapt patterns to suit specific design challenges.

11. Prototyping Techniques:

  • This module introduced students to prototyping tools and techniques, enabling them to create interactive prototypes that simulate the user experience and gather valuable feedback for iteration.

12. Testing Methodologies:

  • Students learned about different testing methodologies, including usability testing and A/B testing, to evaluate the effectiveness and usability of their designs. They gained practical experience in conducting tests and analyzing results.

13. Marketing Strategies Overview:

  • In this session, students explored various marketing strategies and tactics used to promote digital products. They learned how to develop marketing plans and campaigns to attract and engage target audiences.

14. Animation Principles and Practices:

  • During this module, students studied principles of animation and learned how to use animation effectively to enhance user experience and communicate information in digital interfaces.

Closing Thoughts:

Overall, this project provided students with valuable hands-on experience in the field of mobile app design and entrepreneurship. By applying their knowledge and skills to a real-world scenario, they gained insights into the complexities and challenges of bringing a product to market. As their instructor, I was impressed by their creativity, dedication, and growth throughout the process, and I look forward to seeing how they continue to innovate and make a positive impact in the future.

cyberknife-miami.title: Website Redesign: Prostate Cancer Center at CyberKnife Miami
cyberknife-miami.html:
According to DESIGN DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT No 07/ 09/2021 the owner of all intellectual property is Awesomic, Inc.

Problem Statement:

The existing microsite lacked cohesion with the main website's design, resulting in inconsistency in branding and user experience. The redesign aimed to address these issues by implementing the new style of the main website while providing relevant information about the Prostate Cancer Center.

Challenges:

  1. Incorporating the new style of the main website into the microsite design while maintaining brand consistency.
  2. Ensuring that the landing page effectively communicates the services and benefits of the Prostate Cancer Center to visitors.
  3. Implementing client feedback and revisions in a timely manner to meet project deadlines.

Design Process:

The redesign process involved multiple iterations and collaboration with the client to ensure that the new microsite meets their requirements and expectations.

Discovery Phase:

Initial Assessment:

  • Reviewed the existing microsite and identified areas for improvement.
  • Analyzed the new style of the main website provided in the Figma file to understand design elements and branding guidelines.

Define Phase:

Requirements Gathering:

  • Gathered specific requirements from the client regarding the content and functionality of the landing page.
  • Clarified any uncertainties and confirmed design preferences to guide the redesign process.

Ideation Phase:

Wireframing and Prototyping:

  • Created wireframes and prototypes based on the new style of the main website, incorporating client feedback and preferences.
  • Iteratively refined the design to ensure a seamless user experience and alignment with branding guidelines.

Design Phase:

Visual Design:

  • Implemented the new style of the main website, including color scheme, typography, and visual elements, into the microsite redesign.
  • Designed engaging sections and visuals to highlight the services and benefits of the Prostate Cancer Center.

Iterative Design:

  • Collaborated closely with the client to address feedback and make necessary revisions throughout the design process.
  • Ensured that the final design met the client's expectations and reflected the desired brand image.

Final Deliverables:

Completed Redesign:

  • Delivered a visually appealing and informative landing page for the Prostate Cancer Center at CyberKnife Miami.
  • Incorporated the new style of the main website while maintaining brand consistency and usability.

Figma File:

  • Provided a Figma file containing the final design concepts and assets for future reference and implementation.

Takeaways:

Successfully redesigned the microsite to align with the new style of the main website and meet the client's requirements. Implemented client feedback and revisions in a collaborative manner to ensure a satisfactory outcome. Established a cohesive brand identity and user experience for the Prostate Cancer Center at CyberKnife Miami.
